thread:
Sahana Iyer: seeing a flaky failure in the CI integration apply for `redwood-terraform` (matrix job: us-west-2, nat=per_az). It’s failing in `modules/vpc-endpoints` on interface endpoint creation / association. Reruns sometimes go green.

Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-terraform/actions/runs/9133882912/job/25111309219

Log excerpt:
```txt
Terraform v1.6.6
provider[registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws] v5.77.0

module.redwood_private_vpc.module.vpc_endpoints.aws_vpc_endpoint.interface["ecr.dkr"]: Creating...
module.redwood_private_vpc.module.vpc_endpoints.aws_vpc_endpoint.interface["ecr.dkr"]: Still creating... [10s elapsed]
module.redwood_private_vpc.module.vpc_endpoints.aws_vpc_endpoint.interface["ecr.dkr"]: Creation complete after 18s [id=vpce-0f2c1d9b5c4a7c2a1]

module.redwood_private_vpc.module.vpc_endpoints.aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association.interface["ecr.dkr"]: Creating...
╷
│ Error: creating VPC Endpoint Route Table Association (vpce-0f2c1d9b5c4a7c2a1/rtb-0c3e9a5f7d1b8f2aa): InvalidVpcEndpointId.NotFound: The vpc endpoint ID 'vpce-0f2c1d9b5c4a7c2a1' does not exist
│ 	status code: 400, request id: 8d2a6df2-35c6-4a61-b8b2-0a9b2ce6db54
│ 
│   with module.redwood_private_vpc.module.vpc_endpoints.aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association.interface["ecr.dkr"],
│   on .terraform/modules/redwood_private_vpc/modules/vpc-endpoints/main.tf line 214, in resource "aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association" "interface":
│  214: resource "aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association" "interface" {
│ 
╵

Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
```
This looks like AWS eventual consistency (endpoint created, but association API says NotFound). Anyone seen this before / have a preferred fix? :eyes:

Victor Alvarez: yeah that’s classic. The create returns an ID but the next call hits a different backend and it isn’t visible yet. Usually resolves on a second apply.

Question: why are we associating route tables for interface endpoints? (gateway endpoints yes; interface endpoints shouldn’t need rtb associations, they’re ENIs + private DNS). Are we doing this intentionally?

Irene Choi: +1, interface endpoints shouldn’t have `aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association` unless we’re mixing resource types in a single loop.

Can you paste the values in the failing map? Might be our `for_each` includes both gateway + interface and we’re applying RT associations broadly.

Bruno Silva: I dug into the module a bit last week — we have separate resources but they share the same `for_each` keys (`ecr.api`, `ecr.dkr`, etc). The RT association should only be for gateway endpoints, but I think `local.endpoint_route_table_ids` might be non-empty for interface endpoints too when we’re in the “existing VPC adoption” path.

Also: I reran the job locally-ish (same tfvars) and got:
- first apply: same NotFound
- second apply: clean (no changes except it created the association)
So definitely consistent with eventual consistency + we’re calling association immediately.

Nina Petrova: we should avoid relying on “apply twice” as a fix (support will hate it). Two options:
1) remove RT association for interface endpoints (correctness)
2) if we do need it for some reason, add a wait/retry (timeouts or `time_sleep`).

If it’s only in CI integration test harness, a retry at the harness level might be enough, but we should still fix the module logic.

Sahana Iyer: confirmed from the plan output it’s attempting `aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association` for `ecr.dkr`, `ecr.api`, and `logs` (all interface). That seems wrong.

From the run, `endpoint_type = "Interface"` for these, but `route_table_ids` is getting set to the private route tables (same list used by S3 gateway endpoint).

Victor Alvarez: ok then there’s a bug in our locals.

Interface endpoints should be in subnets + SGs; gateway endpoints get route tables. We should split the config structs:
- `interface_endpoints`: name -> { service, subnets, private_dns, security_group_ids }
- `gateway_endpoints`: name -> { service, route_table_ids, policy }

And only create `aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association` for gateway endpoints (or just set `route_table_ids` on the gateway endpoint resource, no separate assoc).

Short-term band-aid: add `depends_on = [aws_vpc_endpoint.interface]` won’t fix this (it already depends implicitly via vpce_id). Need either correct resource graph or stop creating the assoc.

Irene Choi: agreed. Also worth checking if the association resource is even needed for gateway endpoints. AWS provider supports `route_table_ids` inline on `aws_vpc_endpoint` for gateway type.

Less resources == fewer eventual consistency edges.

buildkite-bot: Build #18821 (redwood-terraform / integration-tests) RERUN requested by @sahana

github-actions: Workflow run 9133882912 re-run initiated by Sahana Iyer

Bruno Silva: I can take this. Proposed patch:
- change module to only compute `route_table_ids` for gateway endpoints (S3)
- remove `aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association.interface` entirely

If we still want explicit assoc resources for gateway endpoints, keep it under `gateway_endpoints` only.

Sahana Iyer: :thumbsup: please do. Also, from CI perspective I’ll add a single retry on `terraform apply` for the integration harness anyway (we’ve seen other AWS “NotFound right after create” flukes).

Victor Alvarez: +1 retry in harness is pragmatic, but let’s keep it targeted (only rerun apply once, only on known transient errors). Otherwise we’ll hide real failures.

Maybe match on:
- `InvalidVpcEndpointId.NotFound`
- `DependencyViolation` (sometimes on delete)
- `RequestLimitExceeded`

Irene Choi: pls add a note in the module README / troubleshooting doc too: if customer sees endpoint-related NotFound, they can retry once while we ship fix. But emphasize it shouldn’t be common.

Nina Petrova: do we have an open Linear for this? If not, add one so it’s not lost.

Sahana Iyer: added ENG follow-up in the CI ticket thread and will link the PR once Bruno opens it.

Update: rerun just went green (same commit, same tfvars). So it’s definitely a flake.

Last rerun summary:
- us-east-1 nat=single: pass
- us-west-2 nat=per_az: pass (after rerun)

Bruno Silva: ack. I’ll open PR today w/ module split + remove interface RT associations. Will tag @irene and @victor for review.

Victor Alvarez: thanks. once merged we should see this stop. If it continues, next suspect is private DNS enablement for interface endpoints (AWS sometimes delays). But one thing at a time.

Sahana Iyer: cool. closing the loop once PR lands + I’ll keep the harness retry behind a flag so we can remove later.
